author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty name and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, disregarding letter case; a blank name, or none at all, leaves the directory as it is.
acceptance_criteria: a whole specialty name in any letter case narrows both forms of the directory to the veterinarians holding that specialty
the opening letters of a specialty, rather than the whole name, match no veterinarian on either form
a specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list, not a failure
an empty specialty returns every veterinarian on both forms, and a specialty of only spaces behaves the same way
no specialty at all leaves both forms behaving as they did before filtering existed
the paged form lists the filtered matches a page at a time, and moving between pages keeps the specialty
the machine-readable form carries every veterinarian and their specialties in one document when no specialty is named
a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each one of them
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface
free-text search over veterinarians, which NG-9 still declines
filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: Owner-fixed address contract: /vets.html?specialty=<name> and /vets?specialty=<name>. REQ-VET-003 (machine-readable form reinstated as a supported surface) needs no new production code; existing behavior satisfies it, and criterion 7 pins it. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. Two open questions are recorded in the PRD and no criterion depends on either: whether a visible control follows, and whether spaces around a named specialty are ignored before matching.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: An existing pattern with one adjustment. Both vet routes gain an optional specialty parameter, served by a derived query on VetRepository that mirrors OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) exactly: filter argument plus Pageable, resolved by Spring Data from the method name. No new package, no service layer, no new type, no new dependency. The filter belongs in the repository query, not in the controller over the cached full list - recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-11-specialty-filter-in-the-repository-query.md together with the decision that the filtered reads carry no @Cacheable. docs/system-design.md is updated in this dispatch: the Contracts rows for Vets, VetRepository, and VetController are rewired to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, the Known Defects row declaring the machine-readable route pending removal is deleted (REQ-VET-003 retires it), the vet cache scope is stated under Contracts with an ADR back-link, and Security Context names the new request-derived input. docs/adr/README.md now indexes both 2026-08-11 ADRs.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived reads alongside the existing findAll pair - one paged, one whole - matching a whole specialty name and disregarding letter case. Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController.showVetList takes an optional specialty request parameter, keeps the existing page parameter, and chooses between the unfiltered and filtered repository read. The unfiltered branch stays byte-for-byte the behavior REQ-VET-001 has today.

VetController.showResourcesVetList takes the same optional parameter and fills the existing Vets wrapper from the matching read. Absent or blank keeps the cached findAll() path, so REQ-VET-003 and the caching assertion in PetClinicIntegrationTests.findAll() are untouched.
VetController adds the specialty to the model so the template can carry it; the existing currentPage, totalPages, totalItems, listVets attributes are unchanged.
vets/vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty alongside page. No form, control, or input is added - the filter is a URL contract only (prd-entry non_goals).

patterns.description: Page<Owner> findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) - the derived filtered-and-paged read to copy. Property path plus IgnoreCase gives whole-name case-insensitive equality; StartingWith is what would make it a prefix match, so the plain form is what acceptance criterion 2 needs.

The blank-means-everything branch: a missing search term becomes the broadest search rather than a rejection. Mirror the shape for a blank specialty. Test blankness with StringUtils.hasText only - do not strip. The PRD leaves 'should spaces around a named specialty be ignored' open, and no criterion depends on it; stripping would silently decide it.
findPaginated(int) holds the page size as a local variable and builds the PageRequest. Extend this helper rather than introducing a second paging path.

Pagination hrefs are built today by string concatenation inside a link expression. Move them to the parameterized form - @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} - so Thymeleaf encodes both values. Concatenating a request-derived specialty into the URL string is the shape to avoid.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository. Three acceptance criteria - whole-name case-insensitive match, prefix does not match, a multi-specialty vet appears under each - are properties of the derived query and cannot be observed against a mock. Asserting them there proves only that Mockito returns what it was told.
risks.mitigation: Add a repository-level test against the real H2 schema and seed data (VetRepositoryTests, @DataJpaTest or an addition to PetClinicIntegrationTests). Seed rows support it: radiology is held by vets 2 and 5, surgery by 3 and 4, and vet 3 holds surgery and dentistry both. Keep the controller test for parameter threading, model attributes, pagination links, and the JSON document.

risks.risk: Caching a filtered read would key a Caffeine cache created with no size limit and no eviction on a caller-supplied string, letting any caller grow it without bound.
risks.mitigation: The filtered reads carry no @Cacheable. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-11-specialty-filter-in-the-repository-query.md so a reviewer asking why the sibling methods differ finds the reason.

risks.risk: The specialties table has no unique constraint on name and vet_specialties none on the pair, so two specialty rows sharing a name would return a vet twice and inflate the page count.
risks.mitigation: Seeded data contains no duplicate name. Assert distinctness in the repository test. Do not add a schema constraint in this slice - that is a separate change across three vendor schemas.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is @ManyToMany(fetch = EAGER); a paged query over an eagerly fetched collection can page in memory (HHH000104).
risks.mitigation: This is the existing shape of findAll(Pageable), not something the slice introduces. Verify page contents against real data rather than changing the fetch mode; a fetch-mode change is outside this slice.

risks.risk: Six seeded vets against a page size of five means no specialty has enough matches to span two pages, so the paging-keeps-the-specialty criterion cannot be shown against seed data.
risks.mitigation: Prove it at the controller level, where the stubbed repository can return a PageImpl whose total exceeds one page, and assert the rendered links carry the specialty.

notes: REQ-VET-003 confirmed against the code, as the dispatch asked: VetController.showResourcesVetList (VetController.java:65-72) fills the Vets wrapper from VetRepository.findAll() (VetRepository.java:46), and Vet.getSpecialties() (Vet.java:59-64) is @XmlElement-annotated and name-sorted. Every vet and every specialty in one document, already. No production change is needed for it; criterion 7 lands as a regression test. Basis for this and every resolution claim above: direct reads of the full vet package, OwnerRepository, OwnerController, vetList.html, CacheConfiguration, build.gradle, and the H2 schema and seed scripts. The IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, so no search_symbol citation is available - file reads are the weaker but sufficient basis here, since every claim names a file and line rather than a remembered symbol. Autofix audit: the log carries no design-doc-autofix records. Scope guard for the implementer: the prd-entry non_goals rule out any page control, so no template form, no dropdown, and no new message-bundle key for one; REQ-LANG-002 is unaffected. The controller decides only which repository read to call, which is binding and delegation - it adds no business rule to a controller, so the architecture-principles Web controller row and its checklist item are not further breached.

findings.description: The comment 'null keeps the pagination links free of the parameter when nothing is filtered' is factually wrong. Thymeleaf's @{...(specialty=${specialty})} renders a null model value as an empty parameter, not an absent one, so an unfiltered page's pagination links still read /vets.html?page=2&specialty= — the parameter is not free of anything, only its value is empty. A future reader who trusts this comment will be surprised by the rendered URL and may 'fix' the ternary believing it broke, or misdiagnose the empty-specialty query string as a bug. The implementer's own build-pass notes already recognize this exact rendering, so the comment should say what actually happens instead of what was hoped for.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: theVetDirectoryShouldEncodeASpecialtyThatLooksLikeMarkupInItsPaginationLinks does not pin the encoding its name claims. Its only assertion is a negative one - content().string(not(containsString("\"><script>"))) - which proves the payload did not break out of the href but cannot distinguish 'the specialty was percent-encoded into the link' from 'the specialty never reached the link at all'. A future change that drops specialty from the pagination hrefs, or that renders it only under a condition this test does not hit, leaves the test green while the security property it exists to guard goes unexercised. The sibling test at :146 already shows the stronger shape, asserting the exact rendered href for the benign value. Verified separately that the current production template is sound: the hrefs moved from Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) to the parameterized @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} form, so the value is URL-encoded as a query parameter and then attribute-escaped, and no preprocessing of request-derived text remains in the changed template.
findings.fix: Add a positive assertion alongside the negative one, pinning the encoded link, e.g. .andExpect(content().string(containsString("href=\"/vets.html?page=2&specialty=radiology%22%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E\""))). Keep the not(containsString(...)) assertion; the pair then fails both on a break-out and on a silently dropped parameter.

recommendations: Resource exhaustion, rated LOW and not blocking, but worth recording: because the filtered reads are uncached (correctly - see approved_aspects), an unauthenticated caller varying the specialty name forces a database round trip per request on both routes, where the unfiltered /vets was previously served from the "vets" cache. The JSON route additionally has no Pageable, so a filtered response is bounded only by the size of the table. The ADR names the latency consequence but not this side of the trade. Reachability is real (no authentication exists anywhere in the app, per the system-design Threat Model) but the harm is small: the directory is six seeded rows, the same shape already exists on the uncached owner search, and the fix belongs with the bounded-cache work that open question 5 already tracks. No change requested in this slice; consider adding the observation to the ADR's Consequences.

Supply chain: NOT VERIFIED against the NVD in this review. No OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no CVE match ran - treat the supply-chain check as un-run, not clean. This diff changes no dependency, so its supply-chain surface is unchanged. Resolved versions read from ./gradlew dependencies for a human or CI to close the check: Spring Boot 4.1.0, Spring Framework 7.0.8, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE (thymeleaf-spring6), Jackson (tools.jackson) 3.1.4, Logback 1.5.34.
approved_aspects: No injection reachable through the new input: both new reads are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) resolved to bound JPQL parameters. Swept the change set and src/main/java for string-concatenated queries, @Query with interpolation, Runtime/ProcessBuilder, and file I/O - none introduced.

XSS on the href path is closed by construction, and the change strictly improves on what it replaced: the five pagination hrefs moved off Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), which evaluates its substitution as template expression source, onto @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the parameter value and attribute-escapes the result. Grepped all of src/main/resources/templates for remaining __${...}__ occurrences: every one carries an identifier or an integer, none carries request-supplied text, and none is in this change set. No th:utext and no javascript:/data: URI anywhere in the templates.

The unbounded-cache reasoning holds under inspection, not just on the ADR's word. CacheConfiguration builds the "vets" cache from a bare MutableConfiguration with statistics only - no size limit and no eviction, and its own Javadoc says a size limit must come from the JCache implementation's own mechanism, which nothing supplies. Annotating either new read @Cacheable would therefore have opened a caller-controlled key into an unbounded store: a trivially reachable memory-exhaustion path on a route with no authentication. Leaving the filtered reads uncached is the correct call and the comment on VetRepository points a future reader at the ADR.

Pattern consistency with the neighbouring implementation of the same concern: OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, the codebase's other request-text-driven search, is likewise a derived query and likewise uncached. The new reads diverge from nothing.

No credentials, tokens, or secret-shaped literals in the diff; no logging added, so no log-injection or sensitive-data-in-logs surface; no deserialization, XML, file, or network surface touched. The JSON route's new parameter feeds Jackson 3 (tools.jackson 3.1.4), which has no default typing enabled.

approved_aspects: Round-1 finding resolved, and the implementer's correction is right. Ran ./gradlew test --tests '*VetControllerTests*' - BUILD SUCCESSFUL, so the pinned literal href="/vets.html?page=2&specialty=radiology%22%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E" is the true rendering. My proposed %3C%2Fscript%3E form was wrong: Thymeleaf's @{...} builds the query string through UriComponents, which treats '/' as an allowed character in the query component (RFC 3986 query = *( pchar / '/' / '?' )), so it is left literal.

An unencoded '/' inside a query-parameter value is acceptable here, on both the transport and the sink side. On the wire it is RFC 3986-legal and unambiguous - the '/' cannot start a path segment once the '?' has been seen, and no downstream parser re-splits it. In the HTML sink it is inert: '/' has no meaning inside a double-quoted attribute value, and the characters that would matter ('"', '<', '>') are all percent-encoded, as the pinned literal shows. The one place a bare '/' could bite - '</script' inside a raw-text element terminating it early - does not arise, because the '<' is encoded to %3C, leaving only the harmless text '%3C/script%3E'. No finding.

The assertion pair now does what the round-1 finding asked. content().string(not(containsString("\"><script>"))) fails on a break-out anywhere in the page; content().string(containsString(encodedHref)) fails if the specialty is silently dropped from the pagination href (the rendered link would read /vets.html?page=2 or ...specialty=), if it is dropped only under this test's conditions, or if the encoding weakens. Neither assertion can pass vacuously for the other's failure mode, which was the exact gap in round 1.

The comment no longer overstates what the normalization does.

The four new JSON-route tests add no security surface and close a real gap: the /vets route's new specialty parameter is now exercised for filtered, unfiltered, blank, and no-match cases. All four drive the real MVC dispatch and binding through MockMvc; the filtered ones stub the derived repository query, so the bound parameter still reaches a parameterized JPQL query, not concatenation.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the veterinarian directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Ten files but one module: the vet feature package, its list template, and docs. 70 production lines against 224 test lines, no sensitive paths, no dependency or schema change, and the unfiltered repository reads keep their existing @Cacheable annotations untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: Two things the diff's framing does not prepare you for. First, the unfiltered page's pagination links change shape - the template moves to the @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} form, so every existing link now renders ?page=2&specialty= with an empty value, which the design record called byte-for-byte unchanged and the PRD's done-when calls behaving as before filtering existed. It is functionally inert and a test pins it, but it is a visible URL-contract change to a pre-existing surface. Second, Vet.specialties is @ManyToMany(fetch = EAGER) and the derived query joins that same collection in its where clause; nothing in the suite asserts that a filtered read still returns a vet's complete specialty set, so REQ-VET-001's each-name-and-its-specialties guarantee under a filter rests on Hibernate keeping the filter join separate from the fetch.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real, not tautological.
